title: Choose the visual world for WisePath
question: Sketches now show a 25-page project. The roll assigned Star Atlas; the transit diagram beat it at 9 pages. Keep, switch, or re-roll.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.lineage: Printed star atlases (Norton, Tirion Sky Atlas 2000)
options.thesis: Your path as a chart of the sky you are mapping: studied pages shine, the next one sits in the finder rings.
options.viewport: Top bar with Map/List, search and progress; atlas-blue chart with 25 pages as stars, Focus next / Fit / zoom; side panel with the next page.
options.risk: Label collisions past ~30 pages need a hover/zoom label rule; astronomy is less familiar than transit.

raised.raise: Finder red is spent only on the next page and the primary action, never as decoration.
State is encoded once: the star symbol is the only completion marker on the chart, no extra badges.
The coordinate grid is the real layout armature: stars snap to it, and it can be toggled off.
One directional law: learning order runs left to right across the chart.
In List view the columns never move; only the state cell changes.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Your path as a metro line: pages are stations, completed stops filled, the next stop marked where you are.
materials: coloured line inks at 45 and 90 degrees
options.viewport: Same shell; the map field draws each branch of the path as a coloured line, stations filled when completed, a 'you are here' ring on the next station.
options.case: Still the most familiar form, but at 25 pages, forcing the graph into lines drops real links and invents false ones, and drag-to-reorder fights octilinear routing.
options.risk: Auto octilinear layout of an arbitrary graph has no solid library; the map stops telling the truth about connections.

options.label: Monochrome Product Canon
options.lineage: Software product marketing in one neutral scale
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white with one accent used four times.
options.viewport: Neutral shell, grey graph canvas, one blue accent.
options.case: Reads as a working product but gives learners nothing to identify with; it is the category default.
options.kept: Scarce accent: one colour, spent only where it carries meaning.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every page a catalog number, names coded as colour strips.
options.viewport: Black field, pages as coded entries.
options.case: Hiding names behind codes fights a study tool where the page title is the point.
options.kept: Nothing labelled twice: state lives in one mark.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Pages built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: White grid sheet, pages as grid cells.
options.case: A strong system but it reads as a poster, not a map of connected concepts.
options.kept: The grid as a real, toggleable armature.
options.risk: Connections get lost in the cells.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: A vertical staff read upward, the future always above.
options.viewport: Centre staff with pages as shaped blocks.
options.case: Too foreign for learners; the notation needs its own lesson.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Pages as departures, state cascading flap by flap.
options.viewport: A board of page rows ranked by order.
options.case: A table, not a map; it loses the connections the product exists for.
options.kept: Fixed columns; only state cells change.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A node-editor canvas: rounded page cards, bezier edges, minimap, side panel.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, dotted canvas with page cards and a minimap, details panel on the right.
canonCard.risk: At 25 pages the cards shrink to illegible titles and the minimap becomes mandatory.
